item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Tue Sep 15 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Tue Sep 15 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU (

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Tue Sep 15 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery. item.title: It's On Us: Bystander Intervention Workshop — Tue Sep 15, 6:00 PM — Global & International Studies Building
item.description:
The It’s On Us: Bystander Intervention Workshop is a 90-minute, audience-driven bystander intervention program that teaches students the skills needed to help in situations involving alcohol and drug use that could lead to a sexual assault. Students practice helping in real-life scenarios and discuss how alcohol and drug use influences a person’s ability to give and get consent to engage in sexual activity with another person.
It's On Us is required for all first-year and transfer undergraduate students. You must attend one session to fulfill the requirement.
Instructions:
Those who arrive more than 5 minutes after the start time will NOT be allowed into the session and will need to attend a different session
If this is your assigned workshop but you cannot attend it in its entirety, please RSVP for a different workshop.
If you have concerns about attending due to personal experiences or need to request accommodations, please contact the office at itsonus@iu.edu.

item.title: A Well-Advised Lunch with Shawn Okpebholo and Lina Gonzalez-Granados — Thu Sep 17, 12:00 PM — MERRILL HALL (MUSIC) / MUSIC
item.description:
Students, sign up here >Okpebholo, a two-time GRAMMY nominee and 2024 Chicagoan of the Year in Classical Music, partnered with Pulitzer and GRAMMY-winning librettist Mark Campbell to create this comic chamber opera. Gonzalez-Granados has been praised for her "rich, heartfelt orchestral sound" (Chicago Sun-Times), as well as her dedication to championing new works. Hear firsthand how a new opera moves from composition to the stage, how composers and conductors collaborate throughout the production process, and what it takes to build a career championing contemporary opera. Don't miss this opportunity to hear from two leading artists in the field and get a behind-the-scenes look at the creation and performance ofThe Cook-Off!
Source: IU Jacobs School of Music

item.title: Tobias Center Research Seminar: Prolonged Harm and Legacies of Violence — Fri Sep 18, 12:00 PM — GLOBAL & INTERNATIONAL STUDIES BUILDING
item.description: This installment of the Tobias Center research seminar series, entitled "Prolonged Harm and Legacies of Violence," features Rana Khoury, Assistant Professor of Political Science at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.Abstract: Most refugees live in protracted displacement for years without achieving permanent rights. Civilians live through wars themselves protracted. How do war's victims think and behave when circumstances change? Conflict legacies scholarship conceptualizes violence as discrete exposure and examines its effects on victims after political conditions have stabilized. These approaches overlook prolonged harm: cumulative, mundane, and ongoing hardship that persists beyond episodic violence and shapes how individuals experience change itself. Prolonged harm cumulates across multiple dimensions: psychological, structural, material, and emotional. item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Sat Sep 19 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Sat Sep 19 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU (

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Sat Sep 19 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery. item.title: Embedded Counseling (CAPS) — Mon Sep 21, 8:00 AM — LGBTQ+ CULTURE CENTER
item.description:
Supporting your well-being is an important part of our work at the LGBTQ+ Culture Center. That's why we are proud to partner with Counseling & Psychological Services (CAPS) to provide an embedded counselor in our space every Monday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Mollibeth Penner, LHMCA serves as our embedded counselor and works directly with students connected to the LGBTQ+ Culture Center. To schedule an appointment, please call CAPS (https://healthcenter.indiana.edu/make-appointment/index.html) and let them know you are an LGBTQ+ Culture Center student interested in meeting with Mollibeth at the center. We hope this partnership makes it easier for you to access support in a space where you feel comfortable and affirmed. All Indiana University events, groups, activities, educational, cultural, and historical observances welcome all members of the Indiana University community.

item.title: The Bad Habits of Albert Quint: Queer Labor and Everyday Lives with Author Matthew Cook — Wed Sep 23, 11:00 AM — Kinsey Institute
item.description: Kinsey Institute Guest Lecture Wednesday, September 2311:00 AM - 12:00 PM In-Person, Lindley Hall 328 (Register below) Online via Zoom (Register here (https://iu.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_ZxYcEzJhQWWy2eOWSd-5HQ)) Every night for the first three months of 1937, 23-year-old Albert Quint completed a page of his diary in the house he shared with his working-class parents in rural Wiltshire (England). He described how his shopwork sustained his obsession with cinema and funded the acting classes which he saw as a stepping stone to a career on the stage. Alongside, he alluded to his 'bad habits' and his erotic interest in the soldiers stationed at nearby military bases. Albert's testimony is the cue for this talk, which explores how work – most especially in the service sector, theatre, and armed forces - was practically, aspirationally, and erotically significant to queer everyday lives in inter and post war Britain.
